source: Network-isolated Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME Shell 46.2 in a nested Wayland compositor. Private Xvfb drove the compositor input. Both applications connected as Wayland clients.
launch: Stock signed-out ChatGPT drew its welcome screen. An XTEST pointer click, delivered by the nested compositor to Continue to sign in, invoked an ephemeral XDG HTTPS desktop handler, which execed an original Debian Chromium ELF with an empty session-only profile on the same private display.
identityCheck: The app and XDG launcher PIDs matched their Wayland socket credentials. A separate process in the same PID namespace verified each /proc/PID/exe against its installed binary by device and inode, and read the start tick from /proc/PID/stat. The window observer exposes only object IDs, owner identity and focus.
close: While Chromium owned keyboard focus, a native Ctrl+W on the isolated seat closed its window. The compositor subsequently granted keyboard focus to the same original ChatGPT toplevel. No explicit refocus command was used.
network: Both processes and the callback were in one loopback-only namespace. The test supplied no account data or credentials, issued no callback request, and opened no debugging port or pipe.
scope: This records native ownership, opening, closing and focus restoration on the isolated cloud source. The experiment did not display the second window in Windows or reach an online sign-in page.
